fn combined_parent_usage(
    execution: ParentExecutionUsage,
    parent: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
) -> Result<ParentExecutionUsage> {
    let combined = ParentExecutionUsage {
        spend_usd: execution.spend_usd + parent.total_spend_usd,
        wall_seconds: execution.wall_seconds + parent.total_wall_seconds,
    };
    validate_parent_usage(combined)?;
    Ok(combined)
}

fn remaining_semantic_budget(
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    usage: ParentExecutionUsage,
) -> deadreckon_runtime::SemanticJudgeBudget {
    deadreckon_runtime::SemanticJudgeBudget {
        remaining_spend_usd: Some(job.policy.max_spend_usd - usage.spend_usd),
        remaining_wall_seconds: Some(job.policy.max_wall_seconds as f64 - usage.wall_seconds),
    }
}

fn semantic_budget_exhaustion(
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    usage: ParentExecutionUsage,
) -> Option<(StopReason, String)> {
    if usage.spend_usd >= job.policy.max_spend_usd {
        return Some((
            StopReason::SpendCap,
            format!(
                "approved spend cap was exhausted before semantic judging (${:.6} used of ${:.6})",
                usage.spend_usd, job.policy.max_spend_usd
            ),
        ));
    }
    if usage.wall_seconds >= job.policy.max_wall_seconds as f64 {
        return Some((
            StopReason::WallCap,
            format!(
                "approved wall-time cap was exhausted before semantic judging ({:.3}s used of {}s)",
                usage.wall_seconds, job.policy.max_wall_seconds
            ),
        ));
    }
    None
}

fn semantic_budget_overrun(
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    usage: ParentExecutionUsage,
) -> Option<(StopReason, String)> {
    if usage.spend_usd > job.policy.max_spend_usd {
        return Some((
            StopReason::SpendCap,
            format!(
                "semantic judging exceeded the approved spend cap (${:.6} used of ${:.6})",
                usage.spend_usd, job.policy.max_spend_usd
            ),
        ));
    }
    if usage.wall_seconds > job.policy.max_wall_seconds as f64 {
        return Some((
            StopReason::WallCap,
            format!(
                "semantic judging exceeded the approved wall-time cap ({:.3}s used of {}s)",
                usage.wall_seconds, job.policy.max_wall_seconds
            ),
        ));
    }
    None
}

fn semantic_judge_budget_exhaustion(
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    usage: ParentExecutionUsage,
    dimension: deadreckon_runtime::SemanticBudgetExhaustion,
) -> (StopReason, String) {
    match dimension {
        deadreckon_runtime::SemanticBudgetExhaustion::Spend => (
            StopReason::SpendCap,
            format!(
                "semantic judging exhausted the approved spend cap (${:.6} used of ${:.6})",
                usage.spend_usd, job.policy.max_spend_usd
            ),
        ),
        deadreckon_runtime::SemanticBudgetExhaustion::Wall => (
            StopReason::WallCap,
            format!(
                "semantic judging exhausted the approved wall-time cap ({:.3}s used of {}s)",
                usage.wall_seconds, job.policy.max_wall_seconds
            ),
        ),
    }
}

fn parent_budget_exhausted(
    parent: &mut deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
    stop_reason: StopReason,
    reason: &str,
) -> Result<ParentCompletion> {
    parent.pause_reason = Some(reason.to_string());
    parent.failure_reason = Some(reason.to_string());
    parent.set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), PhaseStatus::Failed)?;
    deadreckon_core::save_state(parent)?;
    Ok(ParentCompletion::BudgetExhausted {
        reason: reason.to_string(),
        stop_reason,
    })

fn require_authority_digest(job: &Job, label: &str, expected: &str, actual: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if expected == actual {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "{label} changed after job {} was approved",
            job.job_id
        ))))
    }
}

fn current_source_revision(cwd: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    let output = deadreckon_core::git::run_git(cwd, &["rev-parse", "HEAD"]).ok()?;
    output
        .status
        .success()
        .then(|| String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
        .filter(|revision| !revision.is_empty())
}

fn build_job_driver_command(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &Job,
    launch: &LaunchInputs,
    executable: &Path,
    attempt: u32,
) -> Result<Command> {
    let command = match job.shape {
        JobShape::Single if attempt == 1 => build_leaf_command(paths, job, launch, executable),
        JobShape::Single => build_leaf_resume_command(paths, job, executable),
        JobShape::Graph | JobShape::LegacyCampaign => {
            build_advanced_command(paths, job, executable)
        }
        JobShape::LegacyChain => {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
                "legacy chain jobs remain process-bound".to_string(),
            )));
        }
    };
    Ok(command)
}

fn release_guarded_child(child: &mut GuardedChild) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let Some(mut release) = child.release.take() else {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe,
            "guarded child was already released",
        ));
    };
    release.write_all(child.release_token.as_bytes())?;
    release.write_all(b"\n")?;
    release.flush()
}

fn apply_durable_scope_root(command: &mut Command, plan: &LaunchPlan) {
    if let Some(scope_root) = plan
        .signals
        .get(super::job::DURABLE_SCOPE_ROOT_SIGNAL)
        .and_then(|value| serde_json::from_value::<PathBuf>(value.clone()).ok())
    {
        command.env("DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT", scope_root);
    }
}

fn build_leaf_resume_command(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job, executable: &Path) -> Command {
    let mut command = Command::new(executable);
    command
        .arg("supervisor")
        .arg("resume")
        .arg(job.job_id.as_ref())
        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home())
        .env(TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV, job.job_id.as_ref());
    command
}

fn build_advanced_command(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job, executable: &Path) -> Command {
    let mut command = Command::new(executable);
    command
        .arg("supervisor")
        .arg("drive")
        .arg(job.job_id.as_ref())
        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home())
        .env(TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV, job.job_id.as_ref())
        .env(
            TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_LAUNCH_PLAN_ENV,
            paths.job_launch_plan(job.job_id.as_ref()),
        );
    command
}

mod tests {
    use deadreckon_sandbox::WorkspaceAccess;

    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn semantic_smoke_response_is_uncertain_and_does_not_consume_worker_steps() {
        let provider = ScriptedSmokeProvider::new();
        let semantic = provider
            .complete(&ProviderRequest {
                workspace_access: WorkspaceAccess::ReadOnly,
                output_schema: Some(json!({ "type": "object" })),
                ..ProviderRequest::default()
            })
            .await
            .expect("semantic response");
        assert!(semantic.content.contains("\"decision\":\"uncertain\""));
        assert!(
            semantic
                .content
                .contains("cannot independently assess whether a goal was achieved")
        );
        assert_eq!(semantic.trace["workspace_access"], "read_only");

        let worker = provider
            .complete(&ProviderRequest::default())
            .await
            .expect("worker response");
        assert!(worker.content.contains("\"tool_call_id\":\"smoke-bash-1\""));
    }
}

fn plan_budget_exhaustion(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    plan_id: &str,
) -> Result<Option<(StopReason, String)>> {
    let event = deadreckon_core::read_plan_events(paths, plan_id)?
        .into_iter()
        .rev()
        .find_map(|event| match event.event {
            deadreckon_core::PlanEventKind::TaskBudgetExhausted {
                dimension, reason, ..
            } => Some((dimension, reason)),
            _ => None,
        });
    Ok(event.map(|(dimension, reason)| {
        let stop_reason = match dimension {
            deadreckon_core::plan::BudgetDimension::Spend => StopReason::SpendCap,
            deadreckon_core::plan::BudgetDimension::Wall => StopReason::WallCap,
        };
        (stop_reason, reason)
    }))
}

The smallest end-to-end home is `crates/deadreckon/tests/watchkeeper_job_ownership.rs`, directly beside:

- `graph_root_mapping_is_repaired_after_creation_crash`
- `campaign_root_mapping_is_repaired_after_creation_crash`
- `assert_root_mapping_recovery`

Those already construct a real durable Job, activate the exact root-creation failpoints, wait for the supervisor, and assert one Job/root identity.

### Test matrix

Add two tests backed by one helper:

```text
graph_root_budget_survives_creation_crash
  - SpendCap
  - WallCap

campaign_root_budget_survives_creation_crash
  - SpendCap
  - WallCap
```

A local `RootBudgetCase` can carry:

```text
expected stop reason
planner cost
planner wall seconds
approved max spend
approved max wall
```

Use values that exhaust only one dimension:

| Case | Planner cost | Planner wall | Max spend | Max wall | Expected |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| spend | 1.25 | 0.25 | 1.00 | 60 | `SpendCap` |
| wall | 0.25 | 2.00 | 1.00 | 1 | `WallCap` |

Use the existing failpoints:

- Graph: `DEADRECKON_TEST_PLAN_FAILPOINT=after_root_plan_saved_before_driver_state`
- Campaign: enable campaign failpoints and select `after_root_campaign_saved_before_driver_state`

### Deterministic smoke accounting

The smoke planner currently bypasses `provider_plan_drafts` at `plan.rs:595-603` and returns `accounting: None`. The normal smoke provider also reports `$0`, while planner wall time would otherwise come from nondeterministic elapsed time.

Add a debug-only integration-test hook in that smoke branch, not in the provider globally. For example:

```text
DEADRECKON_TEST_SMOKE_PLANNER_ACCOUNTING=
  {"cost_usd":1.25,"wall_seconds":0.25}
```

The hook should construct a fixed `PlannerAccounting` with:

- provider `smoke`;
- model `local-scripted-smoke`;
- fixed token counts, preferably `0`;
- supplied finite, non-negative cost and wall values;
- `SpendEstimate.wall_time_seconds` matching the supplied wall value.

It should only be honored under `debug_assertions` and for a smoke planner. Malformed, negative or non-finite values should fail clearly. Normal smoke behavior must remain `accounting: None`.

This location serves both Graph and Campaign because Campaign uses `build_full_plan_tasks_accounted`. Existing failpoint environment inheritance proves the guarded driver receives these variables.

### Common terminal assertions

After waiting for the Job to become terminal:

- projection outcome is exactly `BudgetExhausted`;
- projection stop reason is exactly the case’s `SpendCap` or `WallCap`;
- exactly one Job `BudgetExhausted` event exists;
- zero terminal `Failed` events;
- zero `Blocked` events;
- exactly one terminal event overall;
- every Job event retains the original Job ID;
- exactly one Job directory exists;
- `driver.json` maps the same Job ID to the same root artifact ID;
- embedded root planner accounting contains the injected cost and wall values;
- restored accounting sidecar/event agrees with the embedded snapshot.

Do not assert that Job-level `ChildLinked` is absent: that event represents the root driver itself, not a Graph task or Campaign sub-job.

Do not require a particular Job attempt count or absence of `RetryScheduled`. Recovery may classify from attempt 1 or use one driver retry. The invariant is zero work-child launch and one typed terminal result.

### Graph-specific zero-launch assertions

The root Plan must have:

- `plan_id == job_id`;
- `owner_job_id == job_id`;
- status `Failed`;
- exactly one `PlanEventKind::RootBudgetExhausted`;
- event dimension matching Spend or Wall;
- no `TaskStarted`;
- no `TaskRunDiscovered`;
- every task still `Pending`;
- every task has an empty attempts list;
- every task has `child_run_id == None`.

`RootBudgetExhausted` already exists in `deadreckon-core/src/plan.rs:657`. The classifier helper at `supervisor.rs:2714` currently only recognizes `TaskBudgetExhausted`; the regression should require it to recognize the root variant too.

### Campaign-specific zero-launch assertions

The root Campaign must have:

- `campaign_id == job_id`;
- status `Failed`;
- exactly one `budget_exhausted` Campaign event;
- `stop_reason` matching Spend or Wall;
- `child_launches == 0`;
- no `sub_launch_prepared`, `sub_launched` or `sub_recovered` events;
- every sub-goal remains `Pending`;
- every `sub_plan_id` and `result_run_id` remains `None`;
- no Campaign `launch/` entries were created.

The existing pure tests at `campaign.rs:3662` and `campaign.rs:3691` already prove spend/wall dimension selection without a crash. The new integration matrix proves that the embedded accounting survives the root-save crash window and still prevents all child work.

name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 07:40:58Z)**_

Read-only audit complete. I found no normal Graph or Campaign entry/re-entry path that launches child work after embedded root planner spend or wall time is exhausted. The core budget boundary is enforced before child allocation/launch in normal execution, direct resume, and supervisor recovery.

However, there are two important lifecycle classification gaps.

1. High: a crash after child metadata removal can turn budget exhaustion into `Blocked/LostContainment`

The supervisor removes the child-control sidecar before reconciling the completed attempt at [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:990). If the supervisor or machine dies after line 993 but before budget finalization completes:

- the root Plan/Campaign may already be `Failed` with a valid typed budget event;
- restart recovery returns unchanged because the driver mapping exists and the artifact is no longer `Pending`;
- `advanced_artifact_recoverable` rejects `Failed` artifacts at [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:1068);
- no child sidecar remains;
- the generic fallback records `Blocked/LostContainment` at [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:905).

A narrower version occurs if the crash is between `AttemptStopped` and terminal `BudgetExhausted` in [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:2859).

The merged-artifact case already has restart classification before this fallback, but failed artifacts with typed budget events do not. Restart should classify durable Graph/Campaign terminal evidence before declaring lost containment.

2. High: cancellation can lose a race with budget finalization

A cancellation arriving after `finish_cancel_requested` checks the projection, but before `finish_advanced_budget_attempt` records `AttemptStopped`, can be overwritten:

- `CancelRequested` sets `projection.stop_reason` to cancellation.
- `AttemptStopped` unconditionally replaces it with `SpendCap` or `WallCap` at [job.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/job.rs:524).
- `append_terminal_event` only tests the current projected stop reason at [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:3231).
- It consequently emits `BudgetExhausted`, not `Cancelled`.

This does not launch work, but it violates cancellation precedence. Preserve an outstanding cancellation through `AttemptStopped`, inspect event history rather than only the projection, or serialize final reconciliation under one control lock.

Qualified secondary issue: Campaign interactive replanning has a crash-consistency gap. It writes newly cumulative accounting into the Campaign at [campaign.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/campaign.rs:1853), then writes the matching accounting event. A crash between those writes makes recovery reject the old event/new snapshot mismatch at [campaign.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/campaign.rs:521), producing `Blocked/CorruptHistory`. The current quiet, preapproved durable Campaign driver does not appear able to enter this interactive branch, so this affects foreground/public replanning rather than the present unattended path.

Defense-in-depth concern: root planner accounting is excluded from both immutable ownership digests at [graph_job.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/graph_job.rs:398) and [graph_job.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/graph_job.rs:444). Normal derived snapshots catch ordinary disagreement, but the crash-before-snapshot window treats the embedded value as authoritative. Including accounting in the immutable digest would close the adversarial tampering route.

Safe paths verified:

- missing mapping plus exhausted `Pending` root: mapping is reconstructed and the Job stops with the typed budget reason;
- existing mapping plus exhausted `Pending` root: recovery stops before children;
- direct Graph/Campaign resume rechecks budget before child scheduling;
- Graph `Forked` resume rechecks accounting;
- Campaign execution has a second remaining-budget check;
- budget event written before artifact status update is recovered/classified correctly;
- cancellation already visible before recovery wins;
- missing or corrupt artifacts fail closed without launching children.

Recommended regression tests:

- Graph/Campaign × spend/wall: fail after child sidecar removal and before reconciliation, restart, assert `BudgetExhausted`, not `Blocked`;
- fail between budget `AttemptStopped` and terminal event, restart, assert typed terminal recovery;
- inject `CancelRequested` between cancellation check and budget `AttemptStopped`, assert final `Cancelled`;
- interactive Campaign replan: fail after Campaign write and before accounting-event append, then prove deterministic recovery.

Read-only design complete. One correction first: the cancellation terminal-outcome race I previously reported is already prevented by the fenced event writer. It reloads history under the Job control lock and suppresses non-cancellation events once `CancelRequested` exists at [job_lease.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/job_lease.rs:230). The smallest changes are therefore:

1. Restart classification

Add one readiness helper beside `advanced_artifact_recoverable`:

```rust
fn advanced_artifact_waits_for_parent_reconciliation(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &Job,
) -> Result<bool>
```

It should:

- validate the existing driver mapping and root identity;
- for Graph, return true for `Merged`, `Failed`, or any typed `TaskBudgetExhausted`/`RootBudgetExhausted` evidence;
- for Campaign, return true for `Merged`, `Failed`, `Killed`, or any `budget_exhausted` event;
- use the existing `plan_budget_exhaustion` and `campaign_budget_exhaustion` readers, so there is only one interpretation of typed budget evidence.

Replace the two merged-only checks at [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:846) with this helper. When true, call the existing `classify_advanced_attempt`. This insertion must remain:

- after stored-child adoption/reconciliation;
- before `maybe_schedule_advanced_recovery`;
- before the generic `Blocked/LostContainment` fallback.

If the readiness helper finds malformed persisted evidence, call `fail_advanced_attempt(..., CorruptHistory, ...)` rather than returning an unrecorded error.

This is preferable to adding another terminal writer: `classify_advanced_attempt` already provides cancellation precedence, mapping validation, spend/wall distinction, malformed-history handling, and Graph/Campaign classification.

2. Make budget finalization restart-idempotent

Extract the active-attempt history scan currently inside `finish_cancel_requested` into:

```rust
fn attempt_is_active(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<bool>
```

Reuse it in both `finish_cancel_requested` and `finish_advanced_budget_attempt`.

In `finish_advanced_budget_attempt`:

- append `AttemptStopped` only if the latest attempt has not already stopped;
- retain the returned projection;
- if that projection shows `CancelRequested`, immediately delegate to `finish_cancel_requested(paths, token, Some(&exit))`;
- otherwise append terminal `BudgetExhausted`.

This prevents a restart after `AttemptStopped` from adding a duplicate stop event. It also preserves a clean `AttemptStarted → AttemptStopped → Cancelled` history if cancellation lands before the budget stop obtains the lock.

Do not change the Job reducer to preserve `CancelRequested` across every `AttemptStopped`. The control-lock fence already implements that policy more safely and atomically.

Deterministic tests

Add these near the current advanced-budget tests in `supervisor.rs`:

- `restart_finalizes_persisted_advanced_budget_without_child_metadata`

  Loop Graph/Campaign × SpendCap/WallCap. Create a failed root artifact with typed budget evidence, start attempt 1, leave all child-control files absent, then call `supervise_one_job` using a different boot identity and a nonexistent executable. Assert:

  - outcome is exactly `BudgetExhausted`;
  - stop reason remains spend or wall;
  - one terminal event;
  - one attempt only;
  - no `Blocked`, `RetryScheduled`, or new `ChildLaunchPrepared`;
  - no Plan task or Campaign sub-goal launch evidence.

- `restart_after_budget_attempt_stopped_seals_without_duplicate_stop`

  Use the same matrix, but append the budget `AttemptStopped` before restarting. Assert exactly one `AttemptStopped`, exactly one terminal `BudgetExhausted`, and no retry/blocked/launch events.

- `cancellation_between_check_and_budget_stop_wins`

  Start an attempt, append `CancelRequested` to model cancellation after the caller’s initial check, then call `finish_advanced_budget_attempt` directly. Assert:

  - final outcome is `Cancelled`;
  - no `BudgetExhausted` Job event exists;
  - the post-cancel attempt stop uses `CancelRequested`;
  - exactly one terminal event.

- `cancellation_between_budget_stop_and_terminal_wins`

  Append the budget `AttemptStopped`, then `CancelRequested`, then invoke `append_terminal_event` with `BudgetExhausted`. Assert final `Cancelled`, no budget terminal event, and no duplicate stop.

The tests can reuse `graph_fixture`, `campaign_fixture`, and `claim_started_attempt`. Extracting the typed-budget artifact setup currently duplicated around [supervisor.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:4470) would keep the matrix concise. No new process failpoint is necessary; constructing the exact durable pre-crash state is faster and fully deterministic.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 08:18:50Z)**_

Approved. No blockers found.

- Restart classification is correctly placed after stored-child reconciliation and before retry scheduling and `LostContainment`.
- Cancellation still wins because `classify_advanced_attempt` begins with `finish_cancel_requested`.
- Malformed budget evidence makes the readiness helper return true, then `classify_advanced_attempt` re-reads it and fails closed with `CorruptHistory`.
- `attempt_is_active` correctly ignores lease-reclaim events, so an existing `AttemptStopped` is not duplicated after restart.
- Cancellation before the budget stop produces one cancellation `AttemptStopped` and `Cancelled`; cancellation after the budget stop still converts the terminal event to `Cancelled`.
- The restart matrix covers Graph/Campaign × spend/wall × both crash positions: before `AttemptStopped` and after `AttemptStopped` but before terminal.
- All three focused tests passed.

Residual caveat only: the restart test models removed child containment by starting with no child sidecar and removing the lease checkpoint, rather than creating and deleting a sidecar. That is equivalent at the reviewed entry boundary, but an explicit sidecar deletion would make the test’s intent more documentary.

name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 08:31:59Z)**_

The failure is now localized: the semantic judge used the same `cli:codex` route, but its read-only request deliberately had no session/output directory. The Codex adapter currently makes both the schema file and last-message capture depend on those paths, so it returned the JSONL transport stream as if it were the judge’s JSON answer. I’m checking the configuration and provider tests to distinguish a routing problem from this response-extraction problem.
